summary: Iteration 10 backend feature is NOT implemented in /app/backend/server.py. Expected: Shipment/ShipmentCreate/ShipmentUpdate carry new fields first_vessel_state and second_vessel_state (default 'planned'), update_shipment detects vessel_name change ('changed') or later planned_etd ('delayed'), and _regenerate_comment emits 'Vessel delayed slightly. Now planned ETD DD.MM.' / 'Vessel changed by S/Line. Now planned ETD DD.MM.' clauses (with '(2nd Vessel)' suffix for the 2nd vessel; SOB overrides). Reality: (a) No first_vessel_state/second_vessel_state fields on any model; (b) update_shipment never calls _auto_delayed_comment and never sets vessel-state fields; (c) _regenerate_comment only ever outputs 'Planned ETD X' or 'SOB X' clauses, never 'Vessel delayed slightly' or 'Vessel changed by S/Line'. Live curl walkthrough confirmed the miss.

critical.issue: PATCH {planned_etd:'2026-09-15'} on shipment whose old planned_etd was 2026-09-10 returns comments='...Planned ETD 15.09. Awaiting confirmation of departure.' — expected 'Vessel delayed slightly. Now planned ETD 15.09.' No first_vessel_state field returned at all.

PATCH {vessel_name:'MSC New'} when existing vessel_name='MSC Original' returns comments='...Planned ETD 15.09. Awaiting confirmation of departure.' — expected 'Vessel changed by S/Line. Now planned ETD 15.09.' No first_vessel_state='changed'.
Missing fields first_vessel_state and second_vessel_state (default 'planned'). Downstream logic depending on state cannot function.
Function does not consider vessel_state; emits only 'Planned ETD' or 'SOB' clauses. Needs branches for 'delayed' and 'changed' states, with SOB overriding both.

Does not compare new vs existing planned_etd/vessel_name to set first_vessel_state; does not do same for 2nd vessel; needs elif chain giving 'changed' precedence over 'delayed'. The legacy helper _auto_delayed_comment exists but is never called.

action_items: Add first_vessel_state: str = 'planned' and second_vessel_state: str = 'planned' to Shipment, ShipmentCreate, and ShipmentUpdate (Optional for Update).

In update_shipment: after loading existing, compute state deltas — elif chain: if new vessel_name provided AND existing has value AND differs -> first_vessel_state='changed'; elif new planned_etd provided AND (existing has value and new > existing) -> first_vessel_state='delayed'. Same for 2nd vessel using second_vessel_name / second_vessel_etd. Do NOT downgrade an existing 'changed'/'delayed' back to 'planned' on unrelated PATCHes.

Update _regenerate_comment to accept vessel state: for 1st vessel, if sob_date -> SOB clause (overrides); elif state=='changed' -> 'Vessel changed by S/Line. Now planned ETD DD.MM.' (+ ' (1st Vessel)' when 2nd exists); elif state=='delayed' -> 'Vessel delayed slightly. Now planned ETD DD.MM.'; else -> 'Planned ETD DD.MM.'. Same pattern for 2nd vessel with ' (2nd Vessel)' suffix.
Ensure PATCH that does not touch vessel_name / planned_etd / second_vessel_* leaves state fields untouched so comment retains prior clause (regression case).
Ensure earlier planned_etd (new < existing) does NOT change state (only later triggers 'delayed').
Delete unused _auto_delayed_comment helper OR wire it in — right now it's dead code but tempting to invoke incorrectly.
critical_code_review_comments: Dead code: _auto_delayed_comment (lines ~438-488) is defined but never called from update_shipment. Either remove or integrate.
server.py is now 1057 lines — consider splitting shipments/reports/dashboard into separate modules (>700-line guideline).
In current update_shipment, exclude_none=True prevents clients from clearing fields (e.g., PATCH vessel_name='' to unset). Acceptable but worth documenting.
